deepDiveText: INITIATING COVERAGE 6th Nov 2026 Arihant Capital Markets Limited|Research Analyst SEBI Registration No: INH000002764 1011, Solitaire Corporate Park, Bldg No.10, 1st Floor, Andheri Ghatkopar Link Rd, Chakala, Andheri (E), Mumbai 400093 Inox Wind Ltd CMP: INR 64.80 Rating: BUY Target Price: INR 122 Stock Info BSE 539083 NSE INOXWIND Bloomberg INXW IN Sector Capital Goods Face Value (INR) 10 Mkt Cap (INR Bn) 112.0 52w H/L (INR) 156/55 Avg yearly Vol (in 000’) 13,122 Shareholding Pattern % (As on Mar, 2026) Promoters 44.18% Public & Others 55.82% Stock Performance (%) 1m 6m 12m INOXWIND:NSE -5.7 -39.5 -56.8 Nifty_50 9.9 2.9 -1.9 Abhishek Jain abhishek.jain@arihantcapital.com 022-42254872 Rohan Baranwal rohan.baranwal@arihantcapital.com Inox Wind Ltd Vs Nifty 50 Inox Wind Limited (IWL) is India's second-largest listed domestic wind turbine maker and the main renewable equipment company of the INOXGFL Group. The company designs (under licence), manufactures, supplies, erects, commissions and maintains wind turbine generators (WTGs) for utility-scale, commercial & industrial (C&I), PSU and retail customers. Its work covers the full life of a project, from wind resource study, land and evacuation infrastructure to 20-25 years of O&M through its listed subsidiary Inox Green. In three years, the company has grown from total income of INR 7.6 bn and an EBITDA loss of INR 2.4 bn in FY23 to total income of INR 45.7 bn and EBITDA (incl. other income) of INR 10.6 bn in FY26. It has ~2.5 GW of annual manufacturing capacity across five facilities, ~3.4 GW of cumulative execution (1,700+ turbines) and an order book of ~4.5 GW. Investment Rationale: Order Book at an All-Time High of ~4.5 GW, Giving 2+ Years of Revenue Visibility: The order book reached ~4.4 GW in July 2026, its highest level ever, after the 1.5 GW Inox Clean MoU and a 200 MW repeat order from NLC India. A 100 MW repeat turnkey order from IOCL took it to ~4.5 GW in September 2026, up ~55% from ~2.9 GW at end-FY26, and management sees execution visibility of more than 24-36 months. About 1 GW of the Inox Clean MoU is non-binding, so the firm book is ~3.5 GW, which alone covers ~2.5-3 years of deliveries at the ~1.2 GW we estimate for FY27E. Framework orders from Inox Clean and CESC, repeat PSU orders from NLC India and IOCL, and orders from other IPP and C&I customers give a diversified book that should support execution over the next 4-5 years. In-house orders are on an arm's-length basis and brought INR 3.9 bn of advances in FY26, while repeat PSU awards confirm IWL's standing in open tenders. With a pipeline of over 2 GW and ~2.5 GW of annual capacity, the book backs FY27 guidance of ~INR 80 bn of total income (+75%), against our estimate of INR 65.9 bn. We expect the company to generate ~71% of its FY27E revenue in H2FY27. Balance Sheet Repaired; Net Debt/EBITDA Down to 0.9x from 6.2x: After losses of INR 4.8 bn and INR 6.7 bn in FY22-FY23, IWL has rebuilt its capital base. Net debt fell from INR 21.3 bn in FY23 to INR 9.4 bn in FY26, and net debt to EBITDA from 6.2x in FY24 to 0.9x. Total equity rose more than 3x to INR 76.9 bn, helped by the INR 12.5 bn rights issue in FY26, which also funded the INR 5.6 bn redemption of preference shares. Excluding working-capital loans, debt is now ~5% of capital, against ~36% in FY23. Interest cost fell from INR 3.4 bn to INR 2.0 bn and interest cover improved from -0.7x to 5.3x, taking PAT from a loss of INR 6.7 bn to a profit of INR 4.5 bn and ROCE from -8.5% to 10.7%. The company is close to net cash on its wider definition at INR 0.2 bn. As working capital is released, we expect net cash of INR 9.5 bn in FY28E and INR 26.4 bn in FY29E, with interest cover of 11.0x and ROCE of 14.8% in FY28E. As the repair so far came from equity (CFO of -INR 8.3 bn over FY24-FY26), the next step depends on cash collection. Its multi-GW project pipeline, with ready substations and right- of-way, supports a "plug-and-play" turnkey offer, while new PGCIL/CTU lines due over FY26-FY30 should open further sites. 4.45 MW 4X Turbine to Close the Gap with 5 MW-Class Rivals: The W2E-licensed 4X follows the 3.3 MW platform that drove the FY24-FY26 recovery. Its ~35% higher rating means ~23 turbines per 100 MW instead of ~30, lowering land, foundation and O&M cost per MW. The prototype was erected in August 2026, with ALMM certification and commercial launch targeted by end-CY26. The Barwani blade moulds upgrade has been completed, and the Inox Clean MoU gives the 4X an anchor customer. With rivals already selling 5 MW-class models, a timely launch is key to winning large IPP and FDRE tenders. Product-Led Model Improves Revenue Quality: In FY24, the order book was 100% turnkey EPC, with payments linked to commissioning milestones; connectivity scope and payment terms depend on the project and vary by order type. Under "Vision 2.0", equipment supply rose to 59% of the third-party book in July 2026, against a ~75% target. These orders carry lower realisation than turnkey but are mostly LC- backed and can ship to whichever site is ready first. Gross margin rose to 44.6% in FY26 from 33.6% in FY23. We expect EBITDA margin of 20.8% in FY27E as the mix shifts, rising to 21.5% in FY28E and holding
